state.product: MenteViva, an iOS brain-training app for healthy-to-mild older adults 60+. Purchase channel: an adult child buys it for their aging parent; family progress sharing via CloudKit is a core feature. Built by a solo developer; ongoing content cadence will be slow.

market_evidence.norms: Mainstream brain-training apps (Lumosity, Elevate, Peak, Impulse, CogniFit, BrainHQ) are freemium subscriptions at $35-95/yr with 4.5+ ratings, free tiers of 3-5 games, and aggressive trials. No mainstream app succeeds at one-time pricing.
market_evidence.reviewer_complaints: Cluster on subscription cost / paywall after a few games, repetitive content, and trials that auto-convert.
market_evidence.senior_subscription_aversion: Seniors/caregivers distrust subscriptions; care facilities avoid auto-renewing app purchases entirely. Seniors have the lowest subscription tolerance of any demographic [unverified survey, but consistent with FTC-vintage wariness].

options_context.one_time: One-time $12.99 with Family Sharing: one purchase covers the whole family, fits the adult-child-purchaser channel, dodges subscription fatigue in App Store review, simplifies refunds. Zero recurring revenue; updates funded by new sales only.
options_context.freemium_annual: Cheap annual $24.99 plus generous free tier (3 games free forever): converts the engaged, doesn't alienate the casual, funds ongoing content.
options_context.free_forever: No revenue at all; unsustainable for even a solo dev long-term.
options_context.subscription_monthly: $4.99/month: market-standard shape but highest friction for this audience; auto-renew is exactly what seniors and facilities avoid.

launch_model.instructions: Which launch monetization model best fits this product and audience?

criteria.one_time_1299_family_sharing: Single $12.99 purchase, Family Sharing enabled, no free tier
criteria.freemium_annual_2499: Free tier with a few games forever; $24.99/yr unlocks everything
criteria.free_forever: Completely free, no monetization at launch
